problem: Indoor robot navigation relies on metric or landmark-based geometric maps (SLAM), which depend on low-level structure, are fragile to localization errors, and are hard for humans to interact with. Earlier behavioral approaches used hand-crafted features that were not robust enough.
motivation: Man-made buildings are designed for human navigation, made of corridors, halls and offices, and humans give directions as behaviors like 'cross the hall, take the corridor to the right'. Deep learning now makes robust visual behaviors possible, so a navigation scheme could skip explicit metric localization and work at a semantic level.
key_idea: Represent an office building as a graph whose nodes are semantic places recognized by perceptual behaviors and whose edges are CNN-based navigational behaviors (e.g. cross-corridor, enter-office) mapping images to motor commands, then plan by chaining behavior triplets.
insight: Purely reactive CNN behaviors are enough for most navigation skills (100% success for cf, io, ch, cc), but memoryless ones fail when the view is ambiguous. Out-of-office reached only 67% because the robot sometimes started facing a wall and deadlocked, and restricting the start orientation (oo-b) raised it to 96%, which shows the need for short-term memory. End-to-end mission failures came mainly from missed landmark detections and repeated visual textures.
method: Behavior graph: nodes are semantic places (offices, corridors, halls) and edges are navigational behaviors, stored as <place|behavior|place> triplets; a plan is a path through the triplets (e.g. O1→O8 as oor, cf, chl, cf, ior).

Reactive navigational behaviors: a CNN maps a 160x120 BW image plus a one-hot 3D subgoal vector (left/center/right) to (x, y, θ) velocities; one network can serve several behaviors (cf, oo, io, ch, cc).

Imitation-learning data generation: random 2D office floor plans are rendered as 3D in DeepMind Lab; RRT* (OMPL) on a C-space with cubic-spline smoothing gives expert paths, and a virtual agent records images and actions, with ±5° orientation jitter.
Place detection (pd): a perceptual CNN classifier that identifies whether the current place is an office, corridor or hall.

Memory-based landmark place detection (lmpd): pretrained VGG 7x7 descriptors are embedded with a bilinear function and stored as keys, key-value-memory-network style, with place-IDs as values. At test time cosine similarity gives a softmax over places plus an 'unknown' class, replaced by a hard max, over n=80 wall-picture landmarks.

Behavior switching and execution: the planner picks the ordered behaviors, and detected places or landmarks trigger transitions between behaviors (e.g. detecting the goal office entrance switches cf to io).

setting.backbone: Small CNNs trained from scratch for reactive behaviors and pd, plus a pretrained VGG-Net feature extractor with a trainable bilinear memory for landmark detection
setting.training_data: Synthetic expert demonstrations from DeepMind Lab on randomly generated office floor plans: 150 to 8000 paths per behavior (46k to 260k images) for navigation behaviors, 12.9k images for pd and 38.5k for lmpd
setting.action_space: Continuous velocities (x, y, θ) output by CNN, switched between discrete behaviors
setting.privileged: The behavior graph is extracted directly from the known map configuration, and the landmarks are known and placed at every meaningful place

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 randomly generated maps x 10 office-to-office missions each (1000 missions)
numbers.extra: Graph taken from the known map; out-of-office trained on random initial poses; custom simulator
numbers.evidence: Table II: 100 maps, 10 missions/map, 1000 missions, 8.3 av. steps/mission, Acc. 81.2%

numbers_note: Only a custom simulator benchmark; no standard navigation benchmark. Behavior-level accuracies are in Table I (cf 100%, io 100%, oo 67%, oo-b 96%, ch 100%, cc 100%, pd 98.2%, lmpd 96.7%).
results: On 1000 missions across 100 random office maps, the system reaches the goal office in 81.2% of missions using 8.3 behavior activations on average. Individual behaviors reach 96-100% accuracy except out-of-office, which is 67% (96% with restricted start orientation). No baselines are compared.
limitations: Evaluated only in simplified synthetic office environments with hand-chosen behaviors and known landmark pictures, and the graph is taken from the known map; no real robot.
Memoryless reactive CNNs deadlock in some situations (out-of-office), and landmark detection misses or repeated textures cause mission failures.
No quantitative comparison with SLAM or DRL navigation baselines, and behaviors must be selected manually.
